ai_show_review.summary: Pedal‑steel country set, stellar China>Rider, solid mid‑set jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The concert opens with a three‑song pedal‑steel country mini‑set before diving into classic material. Highlights include a scorching China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider stretch, tight High Time, and the mellow Uncle John's Band → Black Peter transition. The soundboard capture is clean and balanced, making it an easy listen.
ai_show_review.review: On February 7, 1970 at the Fillmore West the Dead surprised the house with a three‑song country & western mini‑set featuring Jerry’s joyous pedal‑steel on “Saw Mill” and a crisp rendition of “Green Green Grass Of Home.” After that warm‑up the band settled into a tight mid‑set: the legendary “China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider” sequence roared with effortless leads, “High Time” kept the momentum high, and a beautifully mellow segue from “Uncle John's Band” into “Black Peter” showcased the group’s dynamic range. While the later portion of the set loses a bit of steam, the overall performance is strong, especially given the solid soundboard source that captures Jerry’s rich guitar tone, Phil’s vocal cameo on “Uncle John’s Band,” and Bob’s lead vocals on “Seasons Of My Heart.” For anyone looking to hear early‑70s Dead with a rare pedal‑steel showcase, this recording stands out as the definitive version of the night.

best_recording.reason: Good soundboard mix with crisp balance, rich guitar tone and clear capture of the pedal‑steel country set.

key_highlights: Pedal‑steel country mini‑set opens the show (Saw Mill, Green Green Grass Of Home).
"China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider" is described as scorching and effortless.
Tight performance of "High Time" and mellow Uncle John's Band → Black Peter transition.
Overall soundboard quality is good with a clean, balanced mix.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s pedal‑steel work on the opening country set and his rich, full‑tone guitar leads throughout are repeatedly praised; his solo in "Uncle John's Band" shows early exploration of new ideas.
band_performance.Phil: Phil contributes a distinct vocal line on "Uncle John's Band"; his bass is solid overall, though some note a boomy quality during the earliest songs.
band_performance.Bob: Bob leads vocals on "Seasons Of My Heart" and engages in lively banter with Jerry before the "China Cat Sunflower" segue.
